facts.statement: The downloadable data underpins the Connected Nations 2025 report.
Ofcom states that the downloads enable year-on-year infrastructure comparisons.
The download set includes fixed-broadband coverage and full-fibre take-up data.
The download set separately includes fixed-broadband performance and mobile-coverage data.
DSIT plans to continue funding Project Gigabit and the Shared Rural Network.
BDUK moved into DSIT's core department on 1 November 2025.
BDUK spending includes Project Gigabit, Shared Rural Network and Superfast Broadband.
DSIT tracks the percentage of premises passed by gigabit-capable broadband.
DSIT tracks outdoor 4G geographic coverage from at least one mobile operator.
DSIT tracks premises with outdoor 5G coverage from at least one mobile operator.
Project Gigabit remains in the Government Major Projects Portfolio.
Project Gigabit targets gigabit-capable broadband for at least 99% of premises by 2032.
Project Gigabit also seeks full coverage as soon as possible.
Government subsidises deployment to non-commercial premises through Project Gigabit.
Project Gigabit excludes premises that are unaffordable or do not represent value for money.
Project Gigabit's recorded start date is 1 April 2021.
Project Gigabit's recorded end date is 31 December 2032.
Project Gigabit's whole-life baseline cost is £5.4 billion.
Project Gigabit is classified as infrastructure and construction.
Project Gigabit's delivery confidence assessment is AMBER.
The Shared Rural Network is a government agreement with four mobile network operators.
The Shared Rural Network achieved 4G coverage across 95% of UK landmass.
The programme reports coverage gains for 280,000 premises and 16,000 km of roads, delivered 12 months early.
Remaining legally binding Shared Rural Network spectrum obligations are due by January 2027, with improvements continuing until then.
